about: THE ONE SOURCE of every customer-facing word about call forwarding. The dashboard renders it (dashboard/forwarding-guide.js); the line-ready and welcome emails are rendered by the self-serve repo, which must copy this file byte for byte and render forwarding-guide.txt's text from it (TODO(owner): self-serve repo). {number} in a sentence is the receptionist number shown as +1 647 555 0142. Inside a code (on, off) it is the number the phone dials, written as codeNumberFormat says (forwarding-guide.txt shows it as {code_number}). Change this file, then run node tests/forwarding-guide.test.js --write to refresh forwarding-guide.txt.
codeNumberFormatTodo: TODO(owner): which number the codes carry. "e164" dials **61*+13653895994**15#; "10digit" dials **61*3653895994**15#. Not tested on a real phone either way; e164 is what shipped first.
intro: Send the calls you don't answer to your receptionist at {number}. Choose how you'd like to set it up:

devices.label: Android (Samsung, Pixel)
devices.todo: TODO(owner): verify these menu names on a real Samsung and a real Pixel before publishing.
steps: Open the Phone app, tap the ⋮ menu, then Settings.
Find Call forwarding. On a Samsung it is under Supplementary services; on a Pixel it is under Calls or Calling accounts. Choose Voice call if asked.
Turn on three of them and set each to {number}: When unanswered, When busy, and When unreachable.
Leave Always forward off, or your phone will never ring.
If it lets you choose a ring time for When unanswered, pick 15 seconds.
devices.note: Menu names differ between models and carriers. If you can't find them, use Dial a code instead.

devices.label: iPhone
devices.todo: TODO(owner): confirm on a real iPhone.
steps: Don't use Settings > Phone > Call Forwarding for this. On iPhone it forwards every call, all the time, so your own phone would never ring.
Use Dial a code instead. It forwards only the calls you don't answer.

how: Open the keypad in your Phone app on the mobile whose calls you want forwarded.
Type the code exactly as shown, then press Call.
Wait for the confirmation message on your screen.

options.label: Forward the calls you don't answer (recommended)
options.detail: Your phone rings for 15 seconds. If you don't answer, your receptionist picks up before voicemail does.

options.label: Forward when busy, unanswered or unreachable, all at once
options.detail: One code for all three. It uses your carrier's own ring time instead of 15 seconds.

check.text: To check: dial *#61#. It should show {number} for unanswered calls.

voicemail.text: If your carrier's voicemail still answers first, ask your carrier to turn voicemail off on your line.

test.heading: Test it
steps: From another phone, call your own number.
Let it ring. Don't decline it: declining sends the call to voicemail, so it isn't a fair test.
After about 15 seconds your receptionist should answer.
test.unverified: We can't see from here whether your forwarding is on, so this test is the way to check.

a: Your carrier's voicemail is answering before the forward. Ask your carrier to turn voicemail off on your line, then test again. A success message after dialing a code doesn't mean voicemail is off.

faq.q: Do I have to turn voicemail off?
a: Usually, yes. If voicemail picks up first, your receptionist never gets the call. With voicemail off, your receptionist takes the message instead.

faq.q: How do I turn it off?
a: Dial ##61#, or ##004# if you used that code. If you used your phone's settings, switch those back off. Turn your voicemail back on if you want it.
The codes are standard, but some carriers need call forwarding added to your plan first, and some charge for forwarded minutes.
Tested on Koodo with an iPhone; other carriers not tested yet.
The codes above are for mobile phones. They will not work on a landline.

A landline is forwarded by the company that provides the line, not from the handset. Ring them and ask for "call forward on no answer" to {number}. Most providers have their own dial code for it, so ask them for it.

An office phone system or internet line (RingCentral, Vonage, 8x8, Google Voice, or a PBX) is set in your provider's admin portal or app. Look for Call Forwarding, Call Handling or Answering Rules, and forward calls that are not answered to {number}, after the last phone in any ring group.
